description: The 'Loch Ness Wellington', recovered from Loch Ness in 1985 and conserved as found; wears code R for R-for-Robert. Built at Brooklands. Confirmed on display Sep 2025.
aliases: R for Robert; Loch Ness Wellington

description: Sultan of Oman's VC10, ex Omani Royal Flight; the last VC10 built at Brooklands to return here. Displayed outside in the Aircraft Park. Confirmed Sep 2025.
aliases: VC-10; G-ASIX; Sultan of Oman; VC10; GASIX

description: Second British pre-production/production Concorde, used for development flying; reassembled at Brooklands from parts stored at Filton and opened to visitors in 2006. Cabin tours available.
BAC One-Eleven development aircraft, converted through Srs 400/475/670 standards; displayed in the Aircraft Park.
aliases: BAC 1-11; BAC 111; One Eleven; BAC 1-11 475; OneEleven; BAC 111 475

description: Vickers Viscount 806 'Viscount Stephen Piercey', ex British European Airways and British Air Ferries; displayed in the Aircraft Park.
Vickers Vanguard converted to Merchantman freighter, ex Air Bridge Carriers; flown into Brooklands in 1996 and displayed in the Aircraft Park.
Vickers Viking 1A 'Vagrant', an early post-war Brooklands-built airliner, displayed in the Aircraft Park.
Vickers Varsity T.1 displayed outside in the Aircraft Park; coded A. Confirmed Sep 2025.
Nose section only of a Vickers Viscount 837 used by the Royal Aircraft Establishment; displayed outside. Confirmed Sep 2025.
Forward fuselage/nose section only of the BOAC VC10 G-ARVM, previously at the RAF Museum Cosford. Presence at Brooklands should be re-checked on site.
Nose section only of a Vickers Valiant B(K).1 built at Weybridge. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Hawker Hurricane Mk IIA in XR-J markings of 71 (Eagle) Squadron; a Brooklands-built airframe. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Hawker P.1127 prototype, the sixth and last built, later used for Harrier development. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Harrier GR.3 modified externally to represent a GR.1. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
The Harrier two-seat company demonstrator G-VTOL, flown worldwide by Hawker Siddeley and British Aerospace. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
BAe Hawk 100 series demonstrator. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Ex Royal Danish Air Force Hunter F.51 displayed inside in 4 Squadron markings and wearing the false serial XF368. Confirmed Sep 2025.
Ex Royal Danish Air Force Hunter F.51. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Fuselage and tail of the Supermarine Swift F.4 world air speed record aircraft. On loan. Confirmed on display inside Sep 2025.
Chipmunk T.10 fuselage held in store; not normally visible to visitors. Last reported Nov 2018.
Flying replica Vickers Vimy built in the USA in 1994 and flown on recreations of the Alcock and Brown, Smith brothers and Cape flights. Replica, not an original airframe.
Full-scale reproduction Hawker Fury I built by Retrotec/Historic Aircraft Collection, displayed in the Hawker connection. Replica.
Flying replica Sopwith Camel F.1 built by Viv Bellamy, registered G-BFCZ. Replica, not an original airframe.
Flying replica Bleriot XI built by Mike Beach representing the type flown at Brooklands from 1909. Replica.
Full-size working replica of the 1908 Roe I Biplane, the aeroplane A.V. Roe flew at Brooklands. Replica.
